h1: The 6 Best Docking Stations with 100W Power Delivery of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six docking stations with 100W or higher power delivery, compared on display support, ports, certification and price.
summary: The Plugable Thunderbolt 4 dock is the best 100W docking station, with certified bandwidth, dual 4K or single 6K output and driverless setup. The Anker Prime brings the largest power budget at 160W max. The WAVLINK covers dual 5K and 4K displays, while the UGREEN and Acer are the low-cost compact picks.
intro: A dock labeled 100W does not always charge your laptop at 100W while it also drives monitors and drives. The headline number is often a shared power budget, and a laptop that wants 90W can end up short once peripherals take their cut. The wording of the listing matters more than the badge.

Our editors reviewed eight docks and ranked six, comparing power rating, display support, certification and port mix. The order rests on wattage claims, port lists and the way owners describe them, with no bench measurements, and prices are buckets. A triple-HDMI dock with mixed refresh rates and a near copy of an Anker model were left out.

products.name: Plugable Thunderbolt 4 Dock (TBT-UDM), 100W Charging
products.verdict: Certified Thunderbolt 4, driverless, and built for new MacBooks.
products.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is a Thunderbolt 4 certified dock rated for 100W power delivery. It supports dual 4K monitors over HDMI or one 6K display, and offers six USB ports, an SD card slot and Ethernet. Setup is driverless on Mac and Windows, and the listing says it is built for M4 and M5 MacBooks. It costs $100 to $200.

It ranks first because certification removes the guesswork that plagues generic USB-C docks. The Anker Prime beats it on power headroom, but it lacks the same certification claim, and the WAVLINK needs drivers.

Buy it for a MacBook or a modern Windows ultrabook that runs two screens. The caveat is that 100W is the ceiling, so power-hungry laptops with large chargers may charge slowly under load.
products.idealFor: Mac and Windows users who want verified Thunderbolt.

products.name: Anker Prime Docking Station, 14-Port, 160W Max Output
products.verdict: The largest power budget and port count here.
products.description:
The Anker Prime is a 14-port dock with 160W max total output, 10Gbps data, dual 4K display support, Ethernet and audio ports. The listing says it works with Dell, HP, Lenovo and more, and it falls in the $100 to $200 range.

The reason for the second slot is that it holds the largest power budget and port count in the ranking, ideal for charging a demanding laptop and a pile of accessories. Its 160W is a total figure shared across ports, not a guaranteed laptop charge, which is why the Plugable's certified approach keeps first place.

Buy it if you need a lot of ports and extra power headroom. The caveat is that 160W is the max total output, so check how much of it actually reaches the laptop port before relying on it.

products.name: WAVLINK USB C Docking Station, 13-in-1, 130W PD
products.verdict: 130W and dual high-resolution displays across Mac chips.
products.description:
The WAVLINK 13-in-1 dock is rated for 130W power delivery and drives dual 5K or 4K displays at 60Hz through DisplayLink. It has two HDMI and two DisplayPort outputs, five USB ports, Gigabit Ethernet and audio, and the listing names M1 through M4 Mac support. It sits in the $100 to $200 range.

The reason for the third slot is that DisplayLink needs a driver and can lag with video, whereas the Plugable and Anker docks need less setup. The dual high-resolution capability is the reason to take it.

Choose it if you run two big monitors from a Mac and need the extra outputs. The caveat is the driver: install it before you depend on the dock, and expect software to be part of the experience.
pros: Works with M1 to M4 Macs
products.idealFor: Mac users wanting two high-res displays.

products.name: Anker Nano 13-in-1 Laptop Docking Station, 100W Max PD
products.verdict: A compact hub with a detachable 6-in-1 section.
products.description:
The Anker Nano 13-in-1 dock offers 100W max power delivery, three displays through two HDMI ports and one DisplayPort, 10Gbps USB-C, three USB-A ports, an SD and TF card reader, Ethernet and audio. A detachable 6-in-1 hub section makes it modular. It is in the $100 to $200 range.

The reason for the fourth slot is that the modular design is clever but the listing is less detailed on certification and exact display limits than the Plugable. Three-monitor support is a draw, though the refresh rates for that combination are not clearly stated.

Pick it for a travel and desk hybrid, where you can leave the full dock at home and carry only the hub. The caveat is that three displays often limit refresh rate, so read the exact combination before planning a triple screen.

products.name: UGREEN 7-in-1 Docking Station Dual Monitor, Revodok Pro, 100W PD
products.verdict: Dual 4K in a small aluminum hub at a low price.
products.description:
The UGREEN Revodok Pro is a compact aluminum 7-in-1 dock with 100W power delivery, dual 4K at 60Hz over HDMI and 10Gbps USB-A and USB-C data ports. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket, the lowest tier in this guide.

It ranks fifth because seven ports is the smallest port count here, and the listing gives no Thunderbolt certification. Its strengths are size and price, since you get dual 4K output in a small aluminum body.

Buy it for a laptop that needs two monitors, a few USB ports and a clean desk. The caveat is that it has no Ethernet listed in the specs, so wired network users should look at the Plugable or Anker models.
products.skipIf: You need Ethernet and many ports.

products.name: Acer Laptop Docking Station, 11-in-1, 100W PD
products.verdict: Three-monitor support at a very low price.
products.description:
The Acer 11-in-1 dock offers 100W power delivery, three-monitor support with an 8K DisplayPort and a 4K at 60Hz HDMI output, 10Gbps data, 1Gbps Ethernet and an SD and TF card reader. It costs $25 to $50.

It ranks last because the listing leaves out certification details and the triple-monitor claim needs careful reading, since refresh rates drop when three screens run. The price is the draw, offering more outputs than many docks at triple the cost.

Buy it if you want three displays on a very small budget. The caveat is that cheap docks with many outputs often share bandwidth, so confirm the supported combination before you plan your layout.

whatMatters.detail: Total wattage is often a shared pool across every port, so a 100W dock may send noticeably less to the laptop once monitors and drives draw power. Look for wording such as laptop charging or upstream power. The Anker Prime lists 160W max total output, the WAVLINK lists 130W PD, and the Plugable lists 100W PD. Compare against your laptop's charger.

Thunderbolt certification guarantees bandwidth, while plain USB-C docks vary widely in what they deliver. It matters most when you run dual high resolution displays and fast external storage together. Search the listing for the word certified. The Plugable TBT-UDM carries Thunderbolt 4 certification, while the UGREEN and Acer list USB-C data speeds instead, so expect less headroom.

DisplayLink adds extra screens through software and needs a driver, and it can lag with video or games. The WAVLINK uses it to reach dual 5K and 4K output. Check whether the listing mentions DisplayLink, and install the driver before depending on the dock for real work, since the extra screens stay dark until it is installed.

Display limits change with the number of monitors, and resolution and refresh rate caps shrink when three screens run. The Plugable TBT-UDM lists dual 4K or one 6K, the Anker Nano lists three displays, and the triple display Plugable runs one at 4K@30Hz. Read the exact combination in the listing, not just the headline count.

Port mix decides what you can connect, and a small dock saves space but limits devices. Count USB-A, USB-C, Ethernet, card readers and audio against your daily gear. The Anker Prime has 14 ports, the WAVLINK has 13 and the UGREEN 7-in-1 has seven. Write down everything what you plug in, then match the list.

faq.q: Will a 100W dock charge my laptop fully?
faq.a: Only if the dock's laptop power matches your laptop. Check your charger rating, and remember a shared pool like the Anker Prime's 160W max is split among devices. The Plugable TBT-UDM and UGREEN list 100W PD, which suits thin laptops but not power-hungry workstations.

Assuming every USB-C dock matches Thunderbolt. The Plugable TBT-UDM is Thunderbolt 4 certified, while the UGREEN and Acer rely on standard USB-C speeds, which can limit display resolution and refresh rate. Look for the word certified in the listing.

faq.q: Is the Plugable worth it over the UGREEN?
faq.a: If you want certified bandwidth and a driverless setup, yes. The UGREEN 10-in-1 is cheaper and handles dual 4K@60Hz with Ethernet, but it lacks Thunderbolt certification and the 6K option. Casual dual 4K users can save; heavy storage and display users should buy the Plugable.

For DisplayLink docks like the WAVLINK, yes, you install a driver before the extra screens work. The Plugable TBT-UDM is described as driverless for Mac and Windows, so setup is faster. Download the WAVLINK driver before you travel with it.

The Anker Nano and Acer list three-monitor support, and the triple display Plugable runs three HDMI outputs. Read the supported resolution and refresh rate combination, because three screens often lower the refresh rate. The triple display Plugable manages only 4K@30Hz on one output.

faq.q: Does it need its own power?
faq.a: Yes. Docks at this wattage ship with a power adapter, into the wall before connecting the laptop. The Plugable TBT-UDM and Anker Prime rely on that supply to pass power through. Use the included adapter, since a weaker brick can cut laptop charging.

finalTake: Choose the Plugable if you want certified Thunderbolt 4 and a quick setup. The Anker Prime is the pick when power headroom matters most, and the WAVLINK handles two high resolution screens through DisplayLink. For tight budgets, the UGREEN fits dual 4K in a small body, and the Acer adds a third monitor. Match the wattage to your laptop charger.
